subject: Different convergence criteria for multilevel model

messages.author: 38a3aacdb5d6f07c
messages.subject: Different convergence criteria for multilevel model
parts:
Hi all,

We are trying to fit this model:


STANDARDIZATION: The covariates x_j were standardized by subtracting the mean in the sample and dividing by country-level standard deviations (this includes areas outside the sample so standard deviations of x_j are not 1 but roughly 0.3). The Cauchy priors are scaled using the population standard deviation in y. This is similar to standardizing the outcome y before fitting the model in Stan.

PARAMETRIZATION: We use the "Matt trick" for tau_q, delta_q, psi_d, theta_j, and alpha_h. See the code.

CONVERGENCE: The model converges according to the all Rhats < 1.05 criterion, but not according to convergence.R. The zip file stan_MVP.zip includes files necessary to run the code below:

library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")
options(mc.cores = 4)

source("dependence.R")
source("convergence.R")
model.3 <- stan_model('MVP Model 3e_SM.stan') 
load("outcome_data")
#fit <- sampling(model.3, data = outcome_data, chains = 6, iter = 1000) 
#save(fit, file = "model.3e")
load("model.3e")
fit 
dependence(fit)
Rhats = as.vector(summary(fit)$summary[,"Rhat"])
sum(Rhats > 1.05, na.rm = TRUE) # this is 0
convergence_test(fit, thin = 5, R = 199) # non-convergence?

QUESTIONS: What re-parametrizations should we look at? Should we change the priors (e.g. switch from Cauchy to Half-Normal)? Should we run the chains longer? 

Thank you so much,
Shira

messages.subject: Re: Different convergence criteria for multilevel model
parts:
Bob, the model was in the giant attachment: 

functions {
  # if each element of z is standard normal, then each element of the result 
  # is Cauchy(location, scale) using the inverse CDF transformation
  vector cauchy_icdf(real[] z, real location, real scale) {
    vector[num_elements(z)] out;
    for (q in 1:num_elements(z)) 
      # Phi(z[q]) ~ Unif(0,1) why not use Uniforms instead of Normals? 
      # Bob Carpenter doesn't think it would make a difference
      # and says I should try it both ways
      out[q] <- location + scale * tan(pi() * (Phi(z[q]) - 0.5)); # see p.193 of stan manual
    return out;
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=0> Q;     # number of countries
  int<lower=0> D;     # number of districts
  int<lower=0> J;     # number of villages
  int<lower=0> H;     # number of households
  int<lower=0> N;     # total number of observations
  int<lower=0> L;     # number of pre-treatment covariates
  real y[N];          # outcome variable of interest
  int z[J];           # treatment indicator
  int country_district[D]; # which country is district d in
  int country[J];     # which country is village j in
  int country_hh[H];  # which country is household h in
  int country_lf[N];  # which country is person i in
  int hh[N];          # which household is person i in
  int jj[H];          # which village is household h in
  int dd[J];          # which district is village j in
  row_vector[L] x[J]; # covariates, all are at the village level
}
parameters {
  #********** "random effects", i.e. modeled coefficients ******************#
  real alpha_h_raw[H];                # primitives for each element of alpha_h
  real theta_j_raw[J];                # primitives for each element of theta_j 
  real psi_d_raw[D];                  # primitives for each element of psi_d
  #******************** Variances at each level ****************************#
  vector<lower=0>[Q] sigma_within_hh_q;
  vector<lower=0>[Q] sigma_within_village_q;
  real<lower=0> sigma_village_raw;    # primitive for sigma_village
  real<lower=0> sigma_district_raw;   # primitive for sigma_district
  #************************* Coefficients **********************************#
  vector[L+2] tau_delta_q_raw[Q];     # primitives for tau_q and delta_q
  real gamma;                         # interaction coefficient
  #**************** Hyperparameter on coefficients *************************#
  vector[L+1] delta;                      # mean of delta_q
  real tau;                               # mean of tau_q
  real<lower=0> sigma_tau_delta_raw[L+2]; # primitives for sigma_tau_delta 
  cholesky_factor_corr[L+2] L_Omega;      # Cholesky factor of Omega
}
transformed parameters {
  real alpha_h[H];
  real theta_j[J];
  real psi_d[D];
  real<lower=0> sigma_village; 
  real<lower=0> sigma_district; 
  vector<lower=0>[L+2] sigma_tau_delta;
  vector[L+1] delta_q[Q]; # includes intercept
  real tau_q[Q];
  { #****************** inverse Cauchy to get variances ********************#
    real mean_sigma_y;
    # FOR NOW USE WITHIN HH + WITHIN VILLAGE VARIANCES FOR SCALING:
    mean_sigma_y <- mean(sigma_within_hh_q) + mean(sigma_within_village_q); 
    sigma_village <- 2.5 * mean_sigma_y * tan(pi() * (Phi(sigma_village_raw) - 0.5)); 
    sigma_district <- 2.5 * mean_sigma_y * tan(pi() * (Phi(sigma_district_raw) - 0.5)); 
    # ask Stan people how to get the function working for 1-dim case so I can rewrite the above
    sigma_tau_delta <- cauchy_icdf(sigma_tau_delta_raw, 0, 2.5 * mean_sigma_y);
  }
  { #**** multivariate Matt trick for each delta_q[q], p.198 Stan manual ***#
    matrix[L+2,L+2] L_Sigma; # Cholesky factor of Sigma
    vector[L+2] tau_delta_q[Q]; # includes intercept
    vector[L+2] tau_delta; # includes intercept
    tau_delta[1] <- tau;
    for (l in 1:(L+1)) tau_delta[l+1] <- delta[l];
    L_Sigma <- diag_pre_multiply(sigma_tau_delta, L_Omega); # = diag_matrix(sigma_delta) * L_Omega
    for (q in 1:Q) {
      tau_delta_q[q] <- tau_delta + L_Sigma * tau_delta_q_raw[q]; 
      tau_q[q] <- tau_delta_q[q][1];
      delta_q[q] <- tail(tau_delta_q[q], L+1);
    }
    # delta_q_raw and delta_q are both arrays of size Q where each element is a vector of length L+1
  }
  for (d in 1:D) { #********* univariate Matt trick for each psi_d[d] ******#
    psi_d[d] <- delta_q[country_district[d]][1] + psi_d_raw[d] * sigma_district; 
  }
  for (j in 1:J) { #******** univariate Matt trick for each theta_j[j] *****#
    theta_j[j] <- psi_d[dd[j]] + x[j] * tail(delta_q[country[j]], L) + 
                tau_q[country[j]] * z[j] + gamma * x[j] * tail(delta_q[country[j]], L) * z[j] + 
                theta_j_raw[j] * sigma_village; 
  }
  for (h in 1:H) { #******** univariate Matt trick for each alpha_h[h] *****#
    alpha_h[h] <- theta_j[jj[h]] + alpha_h_raw[h] * sigma_within_village_q[country_hh[h]]; 
  }
}
model {
  #************************** imply half-Cauchy priors *******************#
  sigma_village_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma_district_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma_tau_delta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  #**************** implies a multinormal prior for each delta_q[q] ******#
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  for (q in 1:Q) tau_delta_q_raw[q] ~ normal(0, 1);
  #********* implies univariate normal priors on each theta_j[j] *********#
  alpha_h_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  theta_j_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  psi_d_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  { #************************** likelihood *******************************#
    real mu_y[N];
    real sigma_y[N];
    for (i in 1:N) {
      mu_y[i] <- alpha_h[hh[i]];
      sigma_y[i] <- sigma_within_hh_q[country_lf[i]];
    }
    y ~ normal(mu_y, sigma_y);
  }
}
